findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test: src/forge/release-notes/v1.2.50.md lists every client-visible change merged since v1.2.49 and the release notes tests pass; nothing else changes
Case: normal use - a client reads the upgrade notes for a repo with one configured tool or an unsigned prototype.
The earlier proof gap remains. `tests/test_release_notes.py:22-45,138-155` checks fixture notes and older release bullets, while `tests/test_release_version.py:81-99` checks the notes' structure rather than their claims. The newly recorded source audit missed current inaccuracies: this line says `workers` selects the explorer family, but `src/forge/intake.py:38-40` calls `repo.worker_family`, which gives a single configured `tools` family precedence at `src/forge/repo.py:820-825`. Line 16 says the default human merge setting waits for a person, but `src/forge/close.py:653-655` uses `repo.merge_setting`, which selects agent merges for unsigned prototypes at `src/forge/repo.py:716-719`. The named automated checks can pass with those statements or the new bullets omitted, and the added audit did not establish their accuracy.

why: The v1.2.50 release notes miss what merged after the first notes were written: the explorer follows the builder, typed approval in Codex chats, review severity and pending-after-merge proof, the Codex cache-safe effort change and chat shortening, the queue runner with its notices and stops, and the settings-fix guide rule.
